zero-card-cloud.name: Zero-Card Cloud
zero-card-cloud.summary: Verified $0 cloud gateways, non-autoregressive decision endpoints, and keyless RAG requiring no credit card.

16vram-64ram.name: 16GB VRAM + 64GB RAM Workstation
16vram-64ram.summary: Zone 1 pure 16GB VRAM dense models paired with Zone 2 64GB DDR5 sparse MoE offloading.

mac-apple-silicon.name: Apple Silicon Mac (Unified Memory / MLX)
mac-apple-silicon.summary: Unified memory local inference via Apple MLX and llama.cpp Metal without a PCIe split.

google-ai-studio.name: Google AI Studio (Gemini 4 Hydrogen & 3.8 Flash)
google-ai-studio.summary: Google's primary card-free developer gateway, now serving Gemini 4 Hydrogen with a 1,048,576-token unified context window, multimodal inputs, and four thinking levels alongside Gemini Decision 1.
google-ai-studio.when_to_use: Default zero-card cloud gateway for multi-step coding agents, full-repository ingestion, and multimodal reasoning.
limitations: Free Tier prompts are used to improve products outside EU/UK/CH; redact credentials and sensitive data.
Search Grounding, Maps Grounding, Batch API, and explicit context caching are paid-tier only on Gemini 4 Hydrogen.
Passing thinking_level=minimal or out-of-range temperature/top_p/top_k returns HTTP 400 on gemini-4-hydrogen.
google-ai-studio.quota: No card: Free Tier (gemini-4-hydrogen 1M unified ctx, implicit caching) + Decision 1 (200 RPM / 10K RPD)

zhipu-bigmodel.name: Z.ai BigModel (GLM-4.7-Flash)
zhipu-bigmodel.summary: Card-free Chinese developer API offering a permanently free MIT-licensed GLM-4.7-Flash endpoint with a 200K context window and 128K output cap.
zhipu-bigmodel.when_to_use: Secondary no-card backup for long-context coding and tool-use loops when Google AI Studio rate limits are reached.
limitations: Only glm-4.7-flash is permanently free; the newer GLM-5.x models are billed and fail on $0 accounts.
zhipu-bigmodel.quota: No card: permanently free GLM-4.7-Flash tier (200K ctx / 128K out)

nvidia-nim.name: NVIDIA NIM Developer Catalog
nvidia-nim.summary: Serverless prototyping catalog hosting rack-scale open-weight models—including 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL—without requiring a credit card.
nvidia-nim.when_to_use: Testing giant 300B-550B open-weight models that cannot fit inside consumer workstation memory.
limitations: Restricted to developer prototyping rather than production traffic, with occasional cold-start queues on large MoEs.
nvidia-nim.quota: No card: ~40 RPM developer prototyping catalog

openrouter-free.name: OpenRouter (:free Routes)
openrouter-free.summary: Unified OpenAI-compatible router aggregating community-sponsored free model endpoints behind one API key.
openrouter-free.when_to_use: Quick model comparisons and light fallback routing across diverse open weights.
limitations: 50 RPD on unverified $0 accounts runs out in roughly three multi-step coding tasks; negative balances return HTTP 402 even on :free routes.
openrouter-free.quota: 20 RPM, 50 RPD ($0 balance) -> 1,000 RPD (>=10 credits balance)

groq-cloud.name: Groq Cloud LPU
groq-cloud.summary: Ultra-low-latency LPU inference offering free tiers for compact LLMs (qwen/qwen3.8-27b, gpt-oss-120b) and high-quota Whisper-Large-v3 speech transcription.
groq-cloud.when_to_use: Sub-second small-prompt JSON routing (<6K tokens) and free audio transcription (2,000 requests/day).
limitations: Strict 8,000 TPM cap on free LLMs causes immediate HTTP 429 failures on 20K-token coding agent prompts.
groq-cloud.quota: No card: LLMs 30 RPM / 1K RPD / 8K TPM; Whisper 2K RPD / 28.8K audio sec/day

cloudflare-workers-ai.name: Cloudflare Workers AI (Clef & Clairic)
cloudflare-workers-ai.summary: Edge inference offering 10,000 daily free Neurons for non-autoregressive Clef decision models and Clairic structured extraction.
cloudflare-workers-ai.when_to_use: Zero-output-token edge classification, moderation, and typed span extraction.
limitations: Legacy Workers AI generative catalog models were hard-retired on Nov 20, 2026 (HTTP 410).

pollinations.name: Pollinations AI
pollinations.summary: Keyless community OpenAI-compatible text and FLUX image endpoint requiring zero signup or authentication.
pollinations.when_to_use: Last-resort keyless fallback for ephemeral sandbox testing where no API keys exist.
limitations: Shared public community service; never transmit private code, credentials, or personal data.
pollinations.quota: Keyless fair-use IP quota (text and image)

firecrawl.name: Firecrawl
firecrawl.summary: Clean webpage-to-Markdown crawler with an agent onboarding skill and low token overhead on OpenBenchmarks.
firecrawl.when_to_use: Converting modern JavaScript-rendered documentation pages into clean Markdown for RAG or research.
limitations: Keyless usage is strictly IP-rate-limited; create a free key for multi-page crawls.

jina-reader.name: Jina Reader (r.jina.ai / s.jina.ai)
jina-reader.summary: Zero-SDK URL prefix service turning web pages and PDFs into clean Markdown, with a matching search prefix.
jina-reader.when_to_use: Instant one-line URL reading in shell scripts and lightweight agents.
limitations: Unauthenticated prefix requests throttle quickly under automated batch loops.
jina-reader.quota: Keyless prefix + 10M free tokens with free API key

exa-search.name: Exa 3.0 Neural Search
exa-search.summary: Semantic web search API built for AI retrieval, renewing $10/month in free credits on the 1st of every month.
exa-search.when_to_use: High-precision web discovery for deep research agents and technical literature scouting.
limitations: Deep research search modes exhaust monthly free credits much faster than Lite searches.
exa-search.quota: No card: $10/mo recurring credits (~2,500 Lite searches)

openalex.name: OpenAlex Academic Graph
openalex.summary: Open scholarly index covering 250M+ academic works, citation graphs, and open-access PDF links with zero API keys required.
openalex.when_to_use: Primary literature review, DOI verification, and academic citation mapping.
limitations: Include ?mailto=you@domain.com in queries to enter the fast polite pool.

qwen3.8-27b.name: Qwen3.8-27B (Dense Vision + Text)
qwen3.8-27b.summary: Apache-2.0 27B dense model serving as the primary 16GB VRAM and Apple Silicon coding backbone, hosting both Hugging Face's RL harness adapters and compact uncensored LoRAs.
qwen3.8-27b.when_to_use: Daily-driver local coding, strict instruction following, and single-backbone multi-LoRA serving.
limitations: On 16GB GPUs, keep quantization at IQ4_XS with Q8 KV cache so weights never spill over PCIe.
Avoid Ollama's /v1/chat/completions endpoint with qwen3.8:27b due to reported hangs; use llama-server or mlx_lm.server.

qwen3-coder-next.name: Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B Sparse MoE)
qwen3-coder-next.summary: Sparse 512-expert Mixture-of-Experts coding model activating only 3B parameters per token, making 80B-class capacity practical in 16GB VRAM + 64GB DDR5 hybrid mode.
qwen3-coder-next.when_to_use: Larger repository reasoning and multi-file refactoring on 16GB GPU + 64GB RAM workstations or 64GB+ Macs.
limitations: Keep -ngl 99 so Attention and KV cache stay on GPU; offload cold experts only via --n-cpu-moe.
qwen3-coder-next.launch_recipe: GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1 llama-server -m Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ngl 99 -fa on -c 120000 --load-mode none --n-cpu-moe 29 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --temp 0

gemma-4.name: Gemma 4 Family (26B-A4B Vision & 12B Tri-Modal)
gemma-4.summary: Fast Apache-2.0 open-weight family offering ~140 tok/s text+vision throughput on 16GB VRAM (26B-A4B) and native local audio understanding (12B).
gemma-4.when_to_use: High-speed local general chat, vision inspection, or local audio analysis.
limitations: Only E2B, E4B, and 12B process audio—the 26B-A4B MoE checkpoint is Text + Vision only.

hermes-4.name: NousResearch Hermes 4 (14B / 4.3-36B Neutral)
hermes-4.summary: Neutral-aligned open-weight models designed to follow operator-defined system prompt policies without baked-in blanket refusals.
hermes-4.when_to_use: Self-hosted deployments where you want predictable operator-controlled behavior rather than abliterated weight surgery.
limitations: Always write explicit safety boundaries in your system prompt if exposing the model beyond solo local use.

inkling-2-mini.name: Inkling 2 Mini (26.4B Looped Transformer MoE)
inkling-2-mini.summary: Experimental looped-layer MoE that iterates its middle 12 layers three times (3.4B base / 5.4B effective active, 1M context), now supported natively in mainline llama.cpp (#32218) alongside Unsloth.
inkling-2-mini.when_to_use: Experimenting with high-efficiency looped coding architectures inside 16GB-18GB memory budgets.
limitations: Published 79.2% SWE-bench Verified and 48.2% DeepSWE v1.1 scores are lab-reported; trails Qwen3.8-27B on strict chat (50% MultiChallenge).
Can enter repetitive debug loops—cap max turns/thinking tokens and run inside a filesystem sandbox.

laya-05.name: Laya 0.5 (Multimodal System-1 Decision Model)
laya-05.summary: Compact non-autoregressive scorer evaluating up to 64 typed decisions in a single forward pass (<100-500ms on CPU/NPU/WebGPU), with v0.5 adding 73,728-token image/audio/video support.
laya-05.when_to_use: Fast zero-output-token tool-safety checks, routing gates, and memory verification without occupying GPU VRAM.
limitations: Threshold decisions on calibrated probabilities rather than raw confidence scores; the optional vegaml-learn add-on is non-commercial.
laya-05.launch_recipe: pip install -U laya && unsloth serve-decision convaiinnovations/laya-typed-decisions --port 8888

qwen-image-2.1.name: Qwen-Image-2.1 (7B DiT Native RGBA)
qwen-image-2.1.summary: Compact 7B diffusion transformer supporting native transparent RGBA output and clean 2048px typography inside 16GB VRAM.
qwen-image-2.1.when_to_use: Non-commercial local design assets, typography, and layered transparent image editing.
limitations: Licensed under Qwen Research (non-commercial); use Apache-2.0 FLUX.2 Klein for commercial production assets.

wan-2.2.name: Wan 2.2 (5B & A14B Open Video)
wan-2.2.summary: Permissive Apache-2.0 open-weight video generation model accelerated cleanly on consumer GPUs through WanGP.
wan-2.2.when_to_use: Commercial-safe local video synthesis on 8GB-16GB NVIDIA workstations.
limitations: Newer Wan 3.0 and Wan 2.6 releases remain closed cloud APIs with no published local weights.
wan-2.2.footprint: 6-15 GB VRAM via WanGP MMGP v4

pi.name: Pi Coding Agent (+ @earendil-works/pi-durable)
pi.summary: Minimal, hackable agent loop (TUI, RPC, and SDK) featuring /tree DAG session branching, a built-in MCP + Codemode JavaScript sandbox, and first-party SQLite crash-resumable checkpoints.
pi.when_to_use: When you want full control over context assembly, clean compaction, and the highest-scoring official target for Hugging Face's RL harness adapters.
limitations: Intentionally omits built-in per-tool approval prompts; always pair with safeagents or an OS sandbox.

deepseek-harness.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
deepseek-harness.summary: Cordis-based agent platform where every subsystem—including the agent loop itself—is a hot-swappable plugin, paired with a read-only-by-default sandbox and sub-agent plugins.
deepseek-harness.when_to_use: Building custom agent loops, interactive Creator Mode plugins, or multi-harness web sessions.
limitations: Fast-moving developer preview (0.2.3-alpha.2); pin plugin versions against breaking interface changes.

hermes-agent.name: Hermes Agent (v0.23.4)
hermes-agent.summary: Persistent autonomous agent featuring cross-session memory, autonomous skill authoring, cron scheduling, Telegram/ACP bridges, and official Hugging Face harness adapter support.
hermes-agent.when_to_use: Always-on background assistants, scheduled research digests, and multi-surface personal operations.
limitations: Does not auto-compact aggressively like Pi by default; cap thinking and context lengths on very large repositories.

opencode.name: OpenCode CLI
opencode.summary: Vendor-agnostic terminal coding interface compatible with local OpenAI-compatible servers and backed by an official Hugging Face Qwen3.8-27B harness LoRA.
opencode.when_to_use: Straightforward terminal software engineering with zero vendor lock-in.
limitations: Monitor context growth during multi-hour sessions; compaction is less aggressive than Pi.

safeagents.name: Hugging Face safeagents Proxy
safeagents.summary: Transparent OpenAI/Anthropic runtime proxy auditing every tool call via fast local scanning (atif-scan, ~10-20ms on Apple Silicon) and optional decision-model judges.
safeagents.when_to_use: Mandatory guard layer between autonomous coding harnesses (or unfiltered local models) and shell/filesystem tools.
limitations: Configure an explicit domain plugin rather than relying on empty defaults.
evidence_notes: Audited 1.3M tool calls and blocked 647 suspicious or reward-hacking calls during Hugging Face's RL adapter training.

qwen38-super-adapter.name: Qwen3.8-27B Rank-96 Super-Adapter (HF Harness Hub)
qwen38-super-adapter.summary: Zero-retraining orthogonal rank-96 merge (PEFT combination_type=cat, weight 0.5) combining Pi, Hermes, and OpenCode RL LoRA adapters on one frozen Qwen3.8-27B backbone.
qwen38-super-adapter.when_to_use: Serving multiple agent harnesses from one frozen 15 GB base model, or running with thinking mode enabled (xhigh).
limitations: When running a single harness with thinking off, prefer its specialist LoRA (e.g., pi 64.0% vs 46.0% on SWE-bench Pro hard-51).
Adapters were trained on BF16 weights; verify GGUF quant fidelity and expect brief pre-tool thinking leakage (arXiv:2610.14270).
Merge weight 0.5 was selected using TB2.1, introducing slight optimistic bias on that benchmark; Hermes specialist shows a mild OOD dip on AutomationBench.
qwen38-super-adapter.footprint: +912 MiB LoRA (+304 MiB for single-harness specialist)
evidence_notes: Per-harness RL updates are nearly orthogonal (cosine similarity ~0.01-0.02), allowing rank concatenation without retraining.
Community testing confirmed transfer onto Qwen3.8 derivatives such as Swift-1.5 and MTP-preserving Apple Silicon MLX builds.

eval_tables.title: Out-of-Distribution Control: 300 AutomationBench Tasks (Non-SWE Agent Loop)

qwen38-super-adapter.launch_recipe: llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-IQ4_XS.gguf --lora Qwen3.8-27B-super-adapter-F16.gguf -ngl 99 -fa on -c 65536 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0

qwen38-abliterated-lora.name: Qwen3.8-27B 26MB Uncensored LoRA (Rank-3)
qwen38-abliterated-lora.summary: Lightweight 26 MB rank-3 LoRA (built on Apple Silicon) removing built-in refusals on top of the exact same frozen Qwen3.8-27B base model.
qwen38-abliterated-lora.when_to_use: Authorized security testing, red-teaming, or unfiltered local experimentation without storing a second 15 GB checkpoint.
limitations: Abliterated adapters cannot refuse destructive tool actions; always isolate behind safeagents and Laya 0.5.

hf-in-harness-rl.name: In-Harness RL Recipe (OpenEnv + Harbor + TRL AsyncGRPO)
hf-in-harness-rl.summary: Reusable reinforcement-learning pipeline that trains LoRAs directly inside unmodified shipping harnesses via a token/logprob capture proxy rather than re-implementing agent loops.
hf-in-harness-rl.when_to_use: Reproducing harness-specific RL on your own private repositories or task benchmarks.
limitations: Requires all-linear LoRA, learning rate 2e-5 (1e-4 collapses rollouts), tool bonus 0.1, and strict exclusion of all-pass/all-fail GRPO tasks.
evidence_notes: openenv validate passed 858 of 1,127 candidate tasks; filtering to tasks the base model solves sometimes (171/442) produced the decisive GRPO reward jump.

llama-cpp.name: llama.cpp (Mainline GGUF Engine)
llama-cpp.summary: Universal CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, and ROCm inference server supporting hybrid MoE offloading (--n-cpu-moe), runtime LoRA loading (--lora), and native Inkling looped layers (#32218).
llama-cpp.when_to_use: Primary local LLM server on NVIDIA workstations and cross-platform CLI deployments.
limitations: --no-mmap is deprecated (migrate to --load-mode none); pass -cuda graphs=0 if partial MoE offloading outputs gibberish.

unsloth-runtime.name: Unsloth Runtime & Studio
unsloth-runtime.summary: Optimized local serving and fine-tuning suite offering fast VRAM-exceeding MoE execution, an Anthropic-compatible local endpoint, Decision API, and OS sandboxes.
unsloth-runtime.when_to_use: Serving Dynamic v3.1 GGUFs, local Laya decision endpoints, or routing Anthropic-protocol clients to local models.
limitations: Keep Studio updated alongside mainline llama.cpp when adopting newly released quantization formats.

mlx-lm.name: Apple MLX (mlx-lm)
mlx-lm.summary: Apple's native unified-memory inference framework delivering ~65 tok/s on 4-bit Qwen3.8-27B super-adapter builds with zero PCIe transfer overhead.
mlx-lm.when_to_use: Primary local serving engine on Apple Silicon Macs (M-series Mac mini, MacBook Pro, Mac Studio).
limitations: Prompt prefill lags dedicated NVIDIA Tensor Cores; 32GB+ unified memory is recommended for comfortable 27B coding sessions.

wangp.name: WanGP v20.12 (MMGP v4 + SageGP 1.0.2)
wangp.summary: Memory-managed local video and image engine whose Extreme Chunker fits 15 seconds of 1080p video into 5.9 GB VRAM while exposing a native MCP interface.
wangp.when_to_use: Running Wan 2.2, LTX-2.5, and Qwen-Image-2.1 on 8GB-16GB consumer GPUs.
limitations: Install WGPKernels 1.5.0 and SageGP 1.0.2 (PyTorch 2.10; Triton 3.6+ required for RTX 50-series adaptive Sage2/3).

frontier.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (552B)
frontier.summary: Asymmetric Causal Encoder-Decoder (8B active in / 16B out) achieving a 1/4 HBM KV cache footprint; watch for smaller open checkpoints adopting this KV compression.
limitations: Exceeds 16GB VRAM + 64GB RAM local memory; accessible via NVIDIA NIM prototyping API.

community.name: obra/superpowers Multi-Harness Discipline Pack
community.summary: Widely adopted 15-skill pack enforcing Brainstorm -> Spec -> Red/Green TDD -> Fresh Subagent -> Verification for 2+ hour autonomous runs across Pi, Hermes, OpenCode, and Claude Code.
limitations: On Hermes Agent, use the Hermes-native tool mapping port rather than raw Claude Code tool names.

community.name: disler/durable-pi Multi-Device Agent Showcase
community.summary: Demonstrates crash-resumable SQLite agent state, atomic shared app state, and live tool hot-swapping on top of Pi.
limitations: First-party @earendil-works/pi-durable is now also maintained directly inside the main Pi monorepo.

community.name: Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-Nomas Walkable Worlds
community.summary: Single-GPU WASD-navigable world generator chained by indie creators with LTX-2.5 for video-conditioned audio prototyping.
limitations: Uses NVIDIA PixelUMM decoder (strictly non-commercial previs and pitch use only).

community.name: Apple Silicon MTP-Preserving MLX Harness Merges
community.summary: Community MLX-6bit and 4-bit merges of Hugging Face's rank-96 super-adapter preserve Qwen3.8's MTP layer, hitting ~65 tok/s on Apple Silicon unified memory.
limitations: Verify checksums and benchmark retention on third-party quantized merges before production use.
